ghs.en: It enters the spinal cord from the shoulder, and travels down the spine until it is delivered to the coccyx.

rows.jp: 下腹部が熱っぽくなる。

ghs.en: Taichi: "Very good, Kiri."
ghs.assessment: いいよ tells Kiri that it feels good. The English instead praises her performance as if issuing an evaluation.

rows.jp: 「んるっ……んん、ん、くちゅ、んふ……はぁぁ」

ghs.assessment: She occasionally pulls or lifts her tongue away. A person does not idiomatically 'distance' a body part in this construction.

rows.en: “Clean the tips of my fingers too.”

ghs.assessment: Taichi tells her to clean his fingertips too. The English makes the fingertips a left-dislocated subject and uses an unexplained plural object 'them.'

highlights.text: The fingertips, too, make them clean.

rows.jp: 「ん……んんん……んふぅ、れろ……ん、ん、ん……は、んふぁ」

ghs.assessment: The affectionate Japanese suffix remains unexplained rather than being represented in English.

rows.en: “No more weapons. You’re better off without them.”

rows.en: “Break that rule, and I think she really will attack you.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Me, I don't really think want to do much to anyone."

ghs.en: Kiri: "You... are serious?"
Taichi: "Yep."

rows.jp: 「それどころか、怪我したみみ先輩にかわってアンテナを組み立てているところだ」

ghs.assessment: The name-plus-status address is left in Japanese morphology rather than represented in English.

Kiri: "...but people... there's none anymore."
ghs.assessment: The plural antecedent requires 'there are none' or 'there isn't anyone.'

rows.jp: 「テレビも映らない。ラジオも。ネットも。電話も」
rows.en: “No picture on TV. Nothing on the radio. No internet. No phones.”

ghs.en: Kiri: "Television doesn't work. Nor radio. Nor the 'net. Nor telephones."

rows.jp: 「何もかも通じなくなって……誰が生きているって言うんですか」
rows.en: “Nothing gets through anymore... So who could possibly be alive?”

ghs.en: Kiri: "Nothing but nothing seems to be conveyed... are you saying someone is still alive?"
ghs.assessment: 何もかも通じなくなって says every means of communication has stopped working or getting through. The English double negative phrase is malformed and 'conveyed' lacks a message or recipient.

ghs.assessment: さえ says the phrase carries even a sweet resonance for him, as an unexpected additional quality. 'Nothing but' says sweetness is its sole quality and reverses the scalar relation.

highlights.text: nothing but a distinctively sweet sound

ghs.en: Taichi: "Forcing the setting against will, gathering seven people with so much hardship, with soothing and coaxing, with blatant lies..."
ghs.assessment: He forcibly arranged the camp and struggled to gather seven people. The English nominalization lacks whose will was opposed and does not form an idiomatic action.

rows.jp: 「あっという間にボロが出て」
rows.en: “And the cracks showed almost at once.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Not even the time to blink the eyes and out came the faults in that attempt."

ghs.en: Kiri threw a look at me that said she was yet discerning something heterogeneous.
ghs.assessment: Kiri looks at him as though he were something alien or abnormal. The English uses a technical adjective for mixed composition, adds 'yet,' and makes her look report an ongoing act of discernment.

highlights.text: a look at me that said she was yet discerning something heterogeneous

Taichi: "You're mistaken."

ghs.en: Taichi: "I wanted everyone to get along again."

Taichi: "It's the truth."

ghs.assessment: He changes the subject of the conversation. English requires the article 'the' and more naturally calls it changing the topic.

rows.jp: 「立派じゃないけど、仲良きことは美しきかな、だ」

rows.en: “People figure out each other’s boundaries through trial and error. Isn’t that what relationships are?”

ghs.assessment: The diminutive Japanese address remains unexplained rather than being represented in English.

ghs.assessment: The Japanese status address remains unexplained rather than being represented in English.
